cli_registry.flag_parse_note: Flag descriptors are JS objects {value:"<...>", description:"..."} (value => takes an argument). One descriptor uses single quotes (tasks status:'"<char>"'); parser handles both. `usage:"sort"` appears once in the bundle but is unrelated app code, not CLI.

argument_shapes_assigned.read: obsidian read [file=<name>] [path=<path>] — file resolves like a wikilink (metadataCache.getFirstLinkpathDest), path is exact; falls back to the active file; throws 'No active file...' when neither given and none active.
argument_shapes_assigned.create: obsidian create [name=<name>] [path=<path>] [content=<text>] [template=<name>] [overwrite] [open] [newtab] — name cannot contain '/'; path is the full file path; extension defaults to md; overwrite/open/newtab are bare booleans.
argument_shapes_assigned.vault: obsidian vault [info=name|path|files|folders|size] — returns one field, or the full info block when info omitted.
argument_shapes_assigned.search: DOES NOT EXIST as a CLI verb (0 handlers). The assignment's assumed `obsidian search` shape is not present in 1.13.7 or 1.14.4.

transport.protocol: client (2nd instance losing requestSingleInstanceLock) connects, writes ONE newline-terminated JSON line {"argv":[...],"tty":bool,"cwd":"..."}, then pipes stdin/stdout; server replies on the same socket and ends.
transport.server: the already-running app's main process serves the socket; will-quit -> unlinkSync(socket)
transport.enable_gate: server checks C.cli before executing: 'Command line interface is not enabled. Please turn it on in Settings > General > Advanced.' — measured obsidian.json: {"vaults":{...},"cli":true} (enabled)
transport.verb_dispatch: renderer window.handleCli(argv): argv[0]=verb (default 'help'); key=value args; bare tokens => 'true'; bare format words (json/tsv/csv) map to format=<word> when the verb declares a format flag; unknown verb => 'Command "X" not found. Did you mean: ...'; missing required flag => 'Missing required parameter: ...\nUsage: <verb> ...'.
transport.tui_mode: when stdin+stdout are TTY and argv empty -> interactive TUI (readline over the same socket; Tab completion from __completions/__files/__commands; commands exit/quit/vault:open <name>; per-command vault=<name> prefix switches target).
transport.vault_selection: argv[0] 'vault=<id-or-name>' or cwd inside a registered vault path
transport.last_arg_specials: last argv obsidian://... => URI processed; 1.14.4 ONLY: last argv an existing filesystem path => 'Opened <path>' (version delta vs 1.13.7)

If the integration later needs the official CLI, the executable path is: app running (socket at /run/user/1000/.obsidian-cli.sock) AND an `obsidian`-named client. On this host the client can only come from Register (broken on this packaging per bundle logic) or a wrapper script that re-execs /usr/bin/obsidian with the subcommand when the app is already running. Wrapper scripts are operator-owned; propose, don't install.

Test doubles can be protocol-faithful now: mock server = unix socket at $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/.obsidian-cli.sock accepting one JSON line {argv,tty,cwd} and replying; mock client = same framing. The 73-verb table (embedded) is the contract for fixture command lists.

A read-only verification script could use: `obsidian vault info=path` (resolves vault root), `obsidian read path=<vault-rel path>` (content), `obsidian file path=...` (metadata) — all read-only verbs, no vault writes. Write verbs (create/append/delete/move/property:set/...) must never be invoked by souji.
